## What The Business Is

Micron Technology Inc. (MU) is a U.S.-based semiconductor memory and storage company focused on DRAM, NAND flash, NOR, high-bandwidth memory (HBM), SSDs, and related advanced packaging. Its business is highly cyclical but is currently being reshaped by AI infrastructure demand, where memory bandwidth, capacity, power efficiency, and supply assurance are becoming strategic constraints for cloud, accelerator, automotive, and edge-AI customers. Micron’s fiscal Q3 2026 call emphasized that AI has elevated memory from a commodity input toward a strategic asset, with the company citing tight DRAM and NAND supply conditions expected to persist beyond calendar 2027. ([investors.micron.com](https://investors.micron.com/node/50671/pdf?utm_source=openai))

## What It Does

Micron manufactures and sells DRAM, NAND, HBM, data-center SSDs, mobile/client memory, automotive memory, embedded storage, and legacy products for industrial, medical, aerospace, and defense markets. In AI servers, its key growth products include HBM, high-capacity DDR, low-power server DRAM, PCIe Gen6 SSDs, and SOCAMM2. In March 2026, Micron said its HBM4 36GB 12-high product designed for NVIDIA Vera Rubin, along with SOCAMM2 and PCIe Gen6 SSDs, had entered high-volume production. ([investors.micron.com](https://investors.micron.com/news-releases/news-release-details/micron-high-volume-production-hbm4-designed-nvidia-vera-rubin?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Positive)

Micron reported record fiscal Q3 2026 results on June 24, 2026: revenue of $41.5 billion, record gross margin of 84.9%, and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $25.11; it guided fiscal Q4 revenue to about $50 billion, gross margin to roughly 86%, and EPS to about $31. The company said DRAM revenue reached $31.3 billion and NAND revenue $9.9 billion, both records, supported mainly by sharply higher pricing and favorable mix. ([investors.micron.com](https://investors.micron.com/node/50671/pdf?utm_source=openai))

A major strategic development was Micron’s disclosure of 16 signed strategic customer agreements across data center, consumer, automotive, and other markets. Management said 14 of the agreements represented about $100 billion of remaining performance obligations at minimum contracted price levels, with projected deposits and related commitments of about $22 billion, mostly cash deposits. The company framed these take-or-pay structures as a way to improve revenue visibility, margin durability, and customer supply assurance through the AI-driven shortage cycle. ([investors.micron.com](https://investors.micron.com/static-files/631b1a32-5537-46ae-8f40-82e42fc79dfe?utm_source=openai))

AI memory demand remains a powerful external tailwind. Recent industry reports continue to point to rising DRAM and NAND contract prices into Q3 2026, though at a slower pace than Q2; this supports Micron’s near-term pricing environment while also confirming that supply remains tight. ([tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/ram/memory-price-surge-begins-to-cool-as-consumers-hit-affordability-limit-ai-demand-still-keeps-dram-and-nand-prices-climbing-through-q3-2026?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)

The same shortage and price surge that are boosting Micron’s results also create cycle risk. Recent market commentary flagged that memory-stock profitability has become unusually high and that a future price normalization could pressure earnings expectations; one report cited DRAM prices up dramatically over the year through June 2026 and noted investor concern after memory shares sold off in early July. ([axios.com](https://www.axios.com/2026/07/06/ai-memory-chips-stocks?utm_source=openai))

Pricing momentum may also be moderating. A recent TrendForce-based report indicated Q3 2026 DRAM and NAND prices were still expected to rise, but at a slower rate than the roughly 60% jumps seen in Q2. That matters because Micron’s fiscal Q3 margin expansion was heavily pricing-driven, and management itself guided that the rate of price increases would moderate in fiscal Q4. ([tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/ram/memory-price-surge-begins-to-cool-as-consumers-hit-affordability-limit-ai-demand-still-keeps-dram-and-nand-prices-climbing-through-q3-2026?utm_source=openai))

Micron is also taking on substantial execution and capital-intensity risk. Management projected fiscal 2026 capital spending of about $27 billion and said quarterly fiscal 2027 capex would be above fiscal Q4 levels as it pulls in clean-room capacity for long-term demand. Large greenfield projects in Idaho, New York, Taiwan, Japan, and Singapore face risks around construction timelines, labor, permitting, energy infrastructure, tool availability, and demand matching. ([investors.micron.com](https://investors.micron.com/static-files/631b1a32-5537-46ae-8f40-82e42fc79dfe?utm_source=openai))

- Record fiscal Q3 2026 (revenue $41.5B, 84.9% GM, EPS $25.11) and Q4 guidance (~$50B revenue, ~86% GM, ~$31 EPS) imply an annualized revenue run-rate near $200B versus $90B TTM.

- Net cash balance sheet (market cap exceeds EV by ~$18.6B) adds a valuation cushion.

## Bear Case
- Earnings are heavily pricing-driven at what looks like a cyclical peak: DRAM/NAND price increases are decelerating (Q3 2026 rises slower than ~60% Q2 jumps), and management itself guided moderation.
- Memory stocks sold off in early July 2026 on normalization fears; historical memory cycles show violent margin mean-reversion, which would compress both FCF and the multiple simultaneously.
- Capex intensity is escalating (~$27B FY26, higher quarterly run-rate in FY27) with greenfield execution risk in Idaho, New York, Taiwan, Japan, and Singapore — this caps FCF conversion even at peak revenue.
- Market cap has already re-rated massively (~$1.06T vs. a 3-year mean of ~$215B), leaving little room for disappointment.

- Capex intensity is climbing ($27B FY26, higher in FY27) with greenfield fab execution risk across five geographies, capping FCF conversion just as pricing normalizes.
- A reversion toward historical memory economics would crush both FCF and the multiple simultaneously; the 3y market-cap mean is only ~$215B, underscoring how far the stock has run.
